title: LRUCache evicts entries that were just read
body:
`LRUCache` in `cachetools/__init__.py` should evict the least
recently *used* entry, where reading an entry counts as a use. Reads
do not update the order, so a hot entry is evicted as if it were
cold:

```python
>>> cache = LRUCache(maxsize=2)
>>> cache["a"] = 1; cache["b"] = 2
>>> cache["a"]
1
>>> cache["c"] = 3
>>> "a" in cache
False   # expected True ("b" is the least recently used)
```

Expected: `cache[key]` and `cache.get(key)` on a present key make it
the most recently used; reading a missing key changes nothing.
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file

source.modifications: reformatted with black (layout and quote style only) to pass the repository formatting check; snapshot adds the injected defect, visible tests and empty package markers

defect: LRUCache.__getitem__ no longer moves the key to the end of the order.
